articles.headline: Allgaier Dominates Late at COTA for Second Win of Season
articles.dek: Justin Allgaier drove away from the field in the closing laps to win the Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas.
articles.body:
Justin Allgaier secured his second win of the NASCAR on JRN O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season on Saturday, dominating the closing stages of the Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas. Allgaier started ninth in the number 7 machine and led 15 of the 38 laps on the road course, crossing the finish line with a commanding 9.787-second margin of victory over Corey Day.

The race ran entirely without caution flags, creating a pure test of tire management and rhythm over 38 laps. Sammy Smith started third and paced the field for a race-high 20 laps before fading slightly in the closing run to finish third. Day worked his way up from a second-place start to take the runner-up spot, while Austin Hill earned the biggest mover honors of the afternoon by charging from fourteenth on the grid to finish fifth.

Brent Crews finished sixth, followed by Sam Mayer in seventh and Brennan Poole in eighth. Ryan Sieg and Parker Retzlaff rounded out the top ten in a clean event that saw just four lead changes among three different drivers. Pole sitter Sheldon Creed struggled to maintain track position and fell back to finish sixteenth.

With the win, Allgaier extends his lead at the top of the championship standings to 98 points. Crews holds second place with 95 points, while Smith sits third with 92 points. Sieg and Blaine Perkins round out the top five in the current standings.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series heads to its next event on the 33-race schedule next weekend, as the sim drivers prepare for another tightly contested battle.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Cut-Line Pressures Mount as O'Reilly Series Tackles First Road Course
articles.dek: An early look at the playoff math shows how the road course battle at COTA impacts the bubble drivers.
articles.body:
The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series arrives at Circuit of The Americas for the third round of the season, marking the first road course test on the schedule. With 22 races remaining before the top-12 Chase field is locked in after race 24, the early standings already reflect tight margins across the board. Every single position on the track carries immediate implications for drivers fighting to avoid the cut-line.

## The Top of the Table Battle

Brent Crews leads the championship standings with 64 points after two races, but his advantage is minimal. Blaine Perkins sits just one point behind in second with 63 points, showing consistent speed that keeps him right on the leader's bumper. Anthony Alfredo holds third with 59 points, while Justin Allgaier and Sammy Smith are deadlocked for fourth with 58 points apiece. Allgaier enters this weekend with maximum momentum after claiming the pole position with a 2:10.416 lap, and the simulator model lists him as the favorite with a 20 percent win probability.

## The Bubble and the Chase Math

The most intense pressure point in the garage sits around the 12th position in points. Brennan Poole currently occupies the 12th spot with 45 points, making him the last driver safely in the projected Chase field. Right behind him is Corey Day in 13th with 43 points. Day already has a win on his resume this season, giving him a distinct advantage if he can break back into the top twelve in points or secure additional victories, but the road course specialist event at COTA presents a volatile variable for drivers trying to protect small points cushions.

## Practice and Qualifying Volatility

Saturday's sessions highlighted how quickly fortunes can change on a road course. Sammy Smith dominated the practice charts by setting the fastest lap at 2:12.184, only to struggle in qualifying and end up starting 36th. Conversely, Justin Allgaier and Austin Hill translated strong practice speeds directly into front-row starting spots. Hill qualified second with a 2:11.085 lap, backing up the garage attention he has drawn heading into the road course swing. With simulator win odds also favoring Brent Crews at 15 percent, Carson Kvapil at nine percent, and Jesse Love at eight percent, the race through the twist and turns of COTA will demand precise braking and clean execution to survive the early-season points scramble.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

articles.headline: Justin Allgaier Captures COTA Pole in O'Reilly Series Qualifying
articles.dek: Justin Allgaier sets the pace ahead of the Focused Health 250 with a fast lap of 2:10.416.
articles.body:
Justin Allgaier secured the pole position for the Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas after laying down a fast lap of 2:10.416 during Saturday afternoon qualifying. The qualifying session took place under clear skies with temperatures at 70 degrees Fahrenheit and a light west wind at six miles per hour. Allgaier leads the 38-car field to the green flag for round three of the 2003 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season.

Joining Allgaier on the front row is Austin Hill, who qualified second with a time of 2:11.085. Jesse Love qualified third at 2:11.096, followed by Carson Kvapil in fourth at 2:11.198 and championship leader Brent Crews in fifth at 2:11.267. Taylor Gray rounded out the top six in qualifying with a lap of 2:11.428.

The qualifying session featured notable shifts from earlier practice results. Sammy Smith, who topped the speed charts in practice with a lap of 2:12.184, encountered difficulties in qualifying and will start 36th on the grid. Austin Green will start 38th alongside him. Meanwhile, points contender Brennan Poole managed a tenth-place starting spot with a lap of 2:11.777.

Pre-race simulator models favor the polesitter heavily for Sunday's event. The model gives Allgaier a 20 percent win probability, the highest in the field. Brent Crews enters the weekend atop the standings with 64 points, holding a narrow one-point margin over Blaine Perkins, who sits second with 63 points. Anthony Alfredo is third in the standings with 59 points, while Allgaier and Smith are tied for fourth with 58 points each.

With 22 races remaining before the Chase cut-line takes effect after race 24, positioning on road courses carries heavy weight for drivers hovering near the bubble. Brennan Poole currently holds the final provisional transfer spot in 12th place with 45 points, while Corey Day sits just outside the cut in 13th with 43 points. The Focused Health 250 gets underway following a clean practice and qualifying weekend for the series.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Chase Cut-Line Math Tightens as O'Reilly Series Hits First Road Course
articles.dek: With two races in the books and 22 remaining before the postseason cutoff, the battle for the final transfer spot is already shaping up as a tight points war.
articles.body:
## Early Season Volatility

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series moves from high-speed superspeedways to the technical turns of Circuit of The Americas for the third round of the season. With just two races completed, the early standings reveal a logjam around the cut line that will define the narrative for the next several months. The top 12 drivers in points after race 24 will make the Chase, creating an immediate premium on consistency.

Brent Crews leads the regular season standings with 64 points, but Blaine Perkins is right behind him with 63. The margin at the top is razor-thin, and the lack of a dominant multi-race winner so far means the mid-pack drivers are staying within striking distance through sheer race-to-race accumulation.

## The Bubble Battle

Looking at the provisional cutoff, Brennan Poole holds the 12th and final transfer spot with 45 points. Just two points behind him sits Corey Day with 43 points. Day already has a win to his name from EchoPark Speedway, but under current series parameters, he still needs to secure sufficient points or additional markers to guarantee his postseason security if multiple winners multiply across the 24-race regular season.

Sam Mayer sits 14th with 41 points, followed by Dawson Cram at 39 and Carson Kvapil at 37. Every position on track during Saturday's Focused Health 250 carries immense weight for these teams as they try to establish momentum early in the year.

## Road Course Wildcard

Circuit of The Americas introduces a completely different discipline compared to Daytona and Atlanta. Drivers like Sammy Smith, who topped practice with a 2:12.184, and Justin Allgaier, who was second quickest at 2:12.307, have an opportunity to separate themselves from the pack. The model views Smith and Allgaier as the primary contenders, giving them each a ten percent win probability.

However, road racing often rewards clean execution and mistake-free afternoon stints over raw one-lap speed. With 38 cars entered and only 22 races left before the reset, the margin for error is shrinking faster than the remaining schedule.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

articles.headline: Sammy Smith Tops COTA Practice Speed Charts Ahead of Focused Health 250
articles.dek: The field prepares for round three of the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season as Sammy Smith sets the pace in Friday practice at Circuit of The Americas.
articles.body:
Sammy Smith laid down the fastest lap in practice for the upcoming Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas. Smith piloted his number 8 machine around the 3.41-mile road course with a lap time of 2:12.184. The session set the stage for Saturday's qualifying and the third round of the 33-race 2026 campaign.

Justin Allgaier finished second on the speed charts with a 2:12.307, followed closely by Carson Kvapil in third with a 2:12.395. Parker Retzlaff and Austin Hill rounded out the top five. Hill enters the weekend amid persistent garage rumors regarding his schedule as the series transitions to its first road course of the season.

Points leader Brent Crews sits eighth on the practice charts after logging a 2:12.823. Crews holds a narrow one-point advantage in the standings over Blaine Perkins, who looks to rebound after finishing runner-up in the opening stretch. Crews enters round three with 64 points, while Perkins trails with 63.

The predictive model lists Smith and Allgaier as the joint favorites to win Saturday's race, each carrying a ten percent win probability. Crews sits at eight percent, while Parker Retzlaff and William Sawalich are each tabbed at six percent. Rajah Caruth rounds out the top tier of model favorites at five percent.

Sawalich already holds a guaranteed spot in the 12-driver Chase field courtesy of his Daytona victory. Meanwhile, drivers on the bubble are searching for speed ahead of qualifying. Brennan Poole currently holds the final transfer spot in 12th with 45 points, just two markers ahead of Corey Day, who sits first on the outside looking in following his victory at EchoPark Speedway.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Austin Hill Garage Rumors Persist As Schedule Shifts To Road Courses
articles.dek: Paddock speculation regarding Austin Hill's equipment continues to circulate as the sim series prepares for Circuit of The Americas.
articles.body:
Whispers in the garage area have followed Austin Hill into the second week of the season. Following a frustrating early exit due to an accident at EchoPark Speedway, sources within the pit lane indicate that conversations regarding future team alignment and equipment focus are ongoing.

While nothing has been officially announced or signed by team principals, paddock insiders suggest that performance on road courses could influence technical partnerships moving forward. Hill finished the EchoPark 250 outside the top 30 after the race-ending incident, placing immediate importance on bouncing back at Circuit of The Americas.

Other teams are also evaluating their driver and crew lineups as the schedule transitions away from superspeedways. Observers note that early-season volatility often prompts garage discussions about engineering direction and development priorities. For now, representatives for major operations maintain that preparations for the upcoming road course weekend remain the primary focus, leaving rumor watchers to wait for official word from team headquarters.
articles.author: Marcy Teague

articles.headline: Corey Day Victory Rewrites Early Chase Cut-Line Math After EchoPark
articles.dek: Corey Day's win at EchoPark Speedway shuffles the provisional playoff grid and puts pressure on the drivers hovering around the top 12.
articles.body:
The second race of the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season delivered immediate shifts in the playoff picture. Corey Day drove the number 17 entry to victory in the Bennett Transport & Logistics 250 at EchoPark Speedway, securing win number one of the year. That single checkered flag changes the arithmetic for the entire field over the next 22 races.

Wins carry massive weight under the 24-race regular season format. William Sawalich locked his spot early with a victory in the Daytona opener. Now Day joins him on the winners list, meaning two slots are provisionally locked by race winners even if they sit outside the top 12 in raw points.

Day currently sits 13th in the standings with 43 points. Brennan Poole holds the 12th and final transfer spot on points alone with 45 points. The gap between missing the postseason and locking in is a mere two points after two rounds of competition.

Brent Crews leads the overall standings with 64 points on the strength of consistency, including a fifth-place finish at EchoPark where he led five laps. Blaine Perkins sits second with 63 points after a ninth-place finish. Neither driver has won yet, relying instead on stage points and clean finishes to build a cushion.

Behind them, the battle for the cutoff is intensifying. Anthony Alfredo holds third with 59 points, followed closely by Justin Allgaier and Sammy Smith tied at 58 points. Ryan Sieg sits sixth with 53 points, and Sawalich holds seventh at 52 points despite his Daytona win.

With the series heading to Circuit of The Americas next for the first road course event of the season, drivers on the wrong side of the cut line need performance gains immediately. The model lists several road course favorites at six percent or five percent win probability, but pacing practice and translating speed into stage points will dictate whether the current bubble drivers can create separation before the summer stretch.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander

articles.headline: Corey Day Wins Bennett Transport & Logistics 250 at EchoPark Speedway
articles.dek: Corey Day powered past Justin Allgaier in a frantic superspeedway dash to capture the victory in Race 2 of the NASCAR on JRN season.
articles.body:
Corey Day won the Bennett Transport & Logistics 250 at EchoPark Speedway on Saturday afternoon after surviving a chaotic 65-lap superspeedway battle. Day wheeled the number 17 entry from his eleventh-starting position to lead 12 laps, ultimately edging Justin Allgaier by just 0.020 seconds at the finish line.

The race featured 36 lead changes among 14 different drivers under clear skies and a hot 100-degree track temperature. Three cautions slowed the field, breaking up the pack racing and creating intense drafting battles through the corners. Pole-sitter Parker Retzlaff led early but faded to finish nineteenth.

Justin Allgaier led a race-high 19 laps and pushed hard on the final restart, coming up inches short of the win in the closing seconds. Anthony Alfredo drove a steady race from ninth on the grid to finish third, leading three laps along the way. Carson Kvapil finished fourth without leading a lap, and Brent Crews rounded out the top five after leading five laps.

Logan Bearden earned the Hard Charger honors by advancing 23 positions from thirty-seventh on the starting grid to finish fourteenth. Attrition played a major role in the closing stages as mechanical failures and accidents claimed several contenders. Austin Hill exited due to an accident, Brandon Jones dropped out with a fuel leak, Lee Pulliam suffered a camshaft failure, and Sheldon Creed retired early.

Brent Crews maintained control of the points standings with 64 points after two rounds of the 33-race season. Blaine Perkins sits second in the standings with 63 points following a ninth-place finish. Anthony Alfredo moved up to third with 59 points, while Allgaier and Sammy Smith are tied for fourth with 58 points each.

The NASCAR on JRN O'Reilly Auto Parts Series heads to its next round next week as the field looks to gain momentum in the early-season points hunt.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Austin Hill Rumors Persist as Garage Looks Ahead to Road Courses
articles.dek: Paddock chatter continues to follow Austin Hill regarding potential future seat availability in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series.
articles.body:
Whispers in the garage area at Daytona International Speedway continue to center on Austin Hill and his prospective plans within the league. While Hill was not among the 38 starters for the United Rentals 300, paddock sources indicate that discussions regarding potential part-time or full-time opportunities remain an ongoing talking point among team executives.

League observers have noted that several mid-tier operations are actively evaluating their driver lineups as the schedule shifts away from superspeedways toward road courses and intermediate tracks. With the Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas looming on the horizon, teams with flexibility in their entries are said to be weighing veteran talent against rising simulator prospects.

Nothing is signed and team representatives have declined to comment on any formal negotiations. However, sources close to the situation suggest that evaluating equipment readiness for upcoming road course and short track dates takes priority for most organizations before any driver announcements are finalized.

For now, the focus across the pit lane remains locked on the current 38-car field as they prepare for the trip to Austin, Texas. Any potential roster additions or developmental seat swaps will likely wait until the opening month of the 2026 season concludes and the baseline competitiveness of each team's chassis package becomes clear.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

articles.headline: Sawalich Strikes Early to Lock Down Playoff Spot at Daytona
articles.dek: William Sawalich capitalizes on a 25th-place start to secure the first playoff berth of the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season.
articles.body:
William Sawalich opened the 2026 season by turning a 25th-place starting position into a trip to victory lane at Daytona International Speedway. The United Rentals 300 saw 38 starters battle through 48 laps under clear skies and cool temperatures. Sawalich led just two laps all afternoon, but he made them count when the checkered flag flew.

By taking the win, Sawalich locks himself into the top 12 for the Chase. The 22 races remaining before the cut-off suddenly look a lot less stressful for the 18-year-old driver and his crew. Meanwhile, the rest of the field is left to sort out the early points standings after just one event in the books.

Blaine Perkins started 11th and led two laps before finishing second by a mere 0.077 seconds. Perkins leaves Daytona second in the standings with 63 points, just one marker behind leader Brent Crews. Crews sits atop the table with 64 points after a quiet, clean run to fifth place from a 29th-place starting spot.

Daniel Dye provided the statistical highlight of the afternoon. Dye charged from the 32nd starting position to finish fourth without leading a lap, earning the biggest mover honors in the 38-car field. Ryan Sieg also showed early speed, pacing the field for 17 laps before finishing eighth.

The battle for the final transfer spot into the Chase is already taking shape. Brennan Poole currently holds the 12th and final transfer position with 45 points. Corey Day sits right on the outside looking in at 13th with 43 points, despite having a previous win on his resume. With 22 races left before the grid narrows to 12 drivers, consistency on superspeedways has given way to the upcoming road course test at Circuit of The Americas.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

articles.headline: Sawalich Wins Daytona Season Opener in Photo Finish
articles.dek: William Sawalich outran Blaine Perkins to the checkered flag by 0.077 seconds to win the United Rentals 300 at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.body:
William Sawalich captured the victory in the NASCAR on JRN O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season opener on Saturday at Daytona International Speedway, edging Blaine Perkins by 0.077 seconds in a frantic dash to the finish.

Sawalich started 25th in the 38-car field and methodically worked his way forward over 48 laps, leading two laps when it mattered most. The victory gives him the early points lead in the win column, positioning the driver of the number 18 machine squarely at the front of the championship fight after the first of 33 races.

Blaine Perkins settled for second place after leading two laps of his own. Perkins started 11th and stayed in the lead draft all afternoon, capitalizing on a clean run to secure a valuable haul of points. Cleetus McFarland drove the number 33 car from an 18th-place start to finish third, leading three laps in the process.

Daniel Dye delivered the performance of the race as the biggest mover of the afternoon. Dye charged from his 32nd starting position to finish fourth without leading a lap, navigating through two caution periods and avoiding the attrition that claimed several other drivers. Brent Crews rounded out the top five after starting 29th.

The race featured 15 lead changes among 12 different drivers. Ryan Sieg led a race-high 17 laps from the eighth starting position, eventually finishing eighth. Parker Retzlaff paced the field for 12 laps and finished seventh. Pole sitter Jesse Love led the field to green but faded late to finish 21st.

Attrition claimed four drivers during the afternoon. Ryan Ellis exited due to an ignition failure, while Mason Maggio, Kyle Sieg, and Josh Williams were listed as retired from the event.

With the season opener in the books, Brent Crews leads the championship standings with 64 points. Blaine Perkins sits second with 63 points, followed by Anthony Alfredo with 59 points, and Justin Allgaier and Sammy Smith tied with 58 points apiece.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series heads to its next round next week as the sim-racing regular season continues.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Sawalich Nips Perkins at the Line to Win Daytona Opener
articles.dek: A last-lap charge off turn four gives William Sawalich the United Rentals 300 victory by 0.077 seconds.
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. - William Sawalich edged Blaine Perkins by 0.077 seconds at Daytona International Speedway on Saturday, taking the season-opening United Rentals 300 in a dash to the line.

Sawalich started 25th and led only two laps in the No. 18, but timed his run off turn four on the 48th and final lap to drag-race Perkins to the checkered flag. Cleetus McFarland finished third, while Daniel Dye charged through the field from 32nd to take fourth. Brent Crews completed the top five.

"We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up," Sawalich said. "When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team."

The 48-lap race featured 15 lead changes among 12 drivers under clear, 51-degree skies. Pole sitter Jesse Love struggled to maintain track position in the draft, eventually sliding back to finish 21st.

Ryan Sieg and Parker Retzlaff did the heavy lifting out front through the afternoon. Sieg paced the field for a race-high 17 laps, while Retzlaff led 12 circuits. Both drivers found themselves shuffled backward during the final cycle of moves, with Retzlaff finishing seventh and Sieg crossing the stripe in eighth.

Perkins led two laps late and appeared positioned to hold off the outside lane entering the tri-oval, but Sawalich found clean air off the bumper of the trailing pack.

"Missed it by less than a tenth," Perkins said. "The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year."

Two cautions slowed the event, keeping the 38-car grid bunched up. Several contenders hit trouble during the afternoon, with four drivers failing to make the finish. Ryan Ellis retired early due to an ignition failure, while Mason Maggio, Kyle Sieg, and Josh Williams pulled out of competition before the final restart.

The attrition and pack racing opened lanes for drivers starting deep in the order. In addition to Sawalich and Crews advancing from outside the top 20, Austin Green surged from 34th to finish sixth, Andrew Patterson went from 35th to ninth, and Sammy Smith rebounded from starting 38th to crack the top 10.

Dye made the biggest climb of the day, gaining 28 positions over 48 laps without pacing a single circuit.

"Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess," Dye said. "We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start."

Sawalich leaves Daytona leading the standings with 40 points and an early win in the bank. Perkins ranks second with 35 points, followed by McFarland with 34, Dye with 33, and Crews with 32. Green (31), Retzlaff (30), Sieg (29), Patterson (28), and Smith (27) round out the top 10.

The series continues its 33-race schedule next week for round two.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: One More Day: Austin Hill Eyes Another Daytona Opener
articles.dek: The NASCAR on JRN Xfinity Series season opens tomorrow at Daytona with Austin Hill chasing his fifth season-opening win in six years.
articles.body:
The wait is nearly over for the NASCAR on JRN Xfinity Series as the field prepares for the United Rentals 300 at Daytona International Speedway. Coverage begins at 5 PM ET on JRN on February 14th, 2026, marking the official start of a new simulated racing campaign.

All eyes point directly at Austin Hill as the green flag approaches. Hill enters the season opener as the driver to beat after dominating Speedweeks over recent years, capturing four of the last five season-opening victories at the historic 2.5-mile superspeedway. His recent history at Daytona establishes him as the undisputed favorite to control the draft and defend his ongoing restrictor-plate dynasty.

With zero races in the books, the standings remain a blank slate, leaving every team on equal footing before tomorrow afternoon. The draft packs, single-file freight trains, and late-race shuffling will dictate who survives the chaotic opening laps and positions themselves for a shot at the trophy.

Teams face their final technical inspections this morning before final practices wrap up. The drivers know the superspeedway drafting dynamics leave zero room for error, and the race on JRN will set the competitive baseline for the entire 2026 season.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

Jesse on row one is massive. The spotter has a clean view into turn one and he won't be trapped in dirty air when the mid-pack accordion happens on lap 15.
Ryan Sieg put the 39 in tenth at 47.210. Good solid starting spot without tearing up equipment. That team builds their own stuff and deserves more respect than these kids renting rides. - D

Poole back in 18th at 47.408 because these spec chassis all drive identical in the turbulence. Back in 1994 a guy could build a better nose in the shop and jump five tenths. Now it is all governed down.
It is Daytona qualifying. The spread between 1st and 20th is four tenths of a second. The pack will reshuffle on lap 3 anyway ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
jeb burton p38 literally dead last what actually happened to the car im sick to my stomach
bro had a 46.939 in practice and then forgot how to run a straight line 💀
he had a massive headwind on his run and the team missed the tape on the nose it is NOT his fault he will pass twenty cars in ten laps watch

p38 is wild 💀

posts.title: Anyone else hitting the betting slips based on practice times?
posts.text: If you looked at practice times to set your fantasy lineup please log off. Sam Mayer topped practice at 46.660 because he drafted off Scott and Gray, then Qualified 7th at 47.130. Don't fall for the draft tow trap.
woke up with a massive headache but still locked in Austin Hill top 3 at plus money. starting P3 at 47.055 is basically a gift for how good that 21 pushes.
Perkins at 47.408 in P19 is the sneaky fantasy value. He was 46.968 alone in practice yesterday without a tow. If he stays clean he gets stage points easily.

Betting slips and fantasy points have ruined how folks talk about Daytona... nobody cares about who can actually wheel the car off four anymore. The points stages give freebies to guys riding in the back. Still the greatest track in the country and nobody can change that.

bro rajah caruth p9 at 47.187 is right there in the mix people sleeping on the 88 fr

three cups of coffee deep and already dreading the commercial-to-green-flag ratio. just let them race through turn two without cutting to a truck commercial.
starting on pole just to finish twenty first is a tough look for the twenty car today. guess we have to go back to the drawing board before next weekend. - b

interviews.quote: We started deep in the pack and had to fight for every inch. Moving up nine spots on a road course with no cautions takes hard racing.
Second is decent for our day, but Allgaier had us covered at the end. We will take the points and go on to the next one.
Our car was hooked up all afternoon. We just had to bide our time, let the race come to us, and once we got out front we could stretch it.
We gave it everything we had on that final lap. Just came up a bumper short, but we will take the solid points day and move on.
Our car took everything we asked of it today. We had to wait for the right moment to make our move and it paid off at the line.
We started way back in thirty-second and just kept finding holes to slip through. Good points day for us.
Hate to lose it by that little, but a second-place finish at Daytona is a great start to the year for this team.
We just kept our nose clean and waited for the right lane to open up off turn four. Car was fast when we needed it.
Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess. We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start.
Missed it by less than a tenth. The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year.

We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up. When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team.

chase.headline: Early Chase Math Holds No Surprises
chase.summary: With just two races in the books, our 2,500 simulated seasons have very little data to process, making most early odds tight. Brent Crews leads with 64 points and a 95 percent Chase projection, closely followed by Blaine Perkins at 63 points and 94 percent.

notes.brent crews: Crews sits at the top with 64 points and a 95 percent projection, though the small sample size means this is mostly baseline speed.
notes.cleetus mcfarland: McFarland holds a 65 percent Chase odd despite only 34 points, outperforming pure points expectation based on early simulation variance.
notes.daniel dye: Dye mirrors McFarland with a 62 percent chance at 33 points, again showing the volatility of a two-race model.
notes.nick sanchez: Sanchez sits down at 9 percent with 33 points, trailing his statistical peers significantly in early projections.

race.headline: COTA Road Course Preview
race.summary: Justin Allgaier is the clear favorite for the Focused Health 250 at Circuit of The Americas with 20 percent win odds. We simply do not have enough road course data yet to name any true dark horses.

notes.justin allgaier: Allgaier tops the win odds at 20 percent heading into the road course.
notes.brent crews: Crews is right behind Allgaier with a solid 15 percent win probability.
notes.william sawalich: Sawalich is expected to run well and carries 6 percent win odds after his recent win.

season.headline: Too Early For Championship Talk
season.summary: We have run two races out of 33, so anyone talking about the title right now is just guessing. Brent Crews and Blaine Perkins lead the early model projections at P3.

notes.brent crews: Crews is projected P3 with 745 points and 27 percent title odds in the early model.
notes.blaine perkins: Perkins matches Crews at projected P3 with 740 points and 25 percent title odds.
notes.william sawalich: Sawalich sits down at P11 with 639 points and 1 percent title odds, but his recent win execution proves he can close.
notes.cleetus mcfarland: McFarland lands at projected P9 with 657 points and 2 percent title odds in the current simulation pass.
